newsitem.title: USA: US spot propane continues retracement late in day.
newsitem.headline: US spot propane continues retracement late in day.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices continued sliding by late Tuesday, falling as much as 14 cents in the Midwest and five cents in the Gulf Coast in a retracement from strong Monday gains, players said.

Conway, Kansas, spot propane was offered at about 96 cents a gallon by late afternoon after being traded during the day at amounts ranging from 92 cents to as high as 98 cents -- contrasted with a high of $1.10 on Monday.
Mont Belvieu, Texas, material was offered at 65.50 cents, versus about 70.50 cents yesterday, coming down in sympathy with lower Midwest prices, players said.

Prices had zoomed Monday amid predictions that an artic air mass from Siberia would create much below normal temperatures by midweek in the Midwest and last possibly through the first half of January.
"People have gotten used to the cold weather coming, they're not panicking today," one trader said, adding they were instead "taking profits in both markets."
"There is very little getting done," another trader said, adding, "Most people are taking a breather after yesterday."
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631
